summary:
North Maluku stands under Indonesia's national framework. No province-level law, ordinance, enforcement action or institution specific to North Maluku appears in the reporting reviewed, and the province is not among those that criminalise same-sex conduct under provincial religious law. The national assessment therefore applies here without a provincial addition.

Reported trans-specific violence, police raids and prosecutions in Indonesia are not attributed to North Maluku in the available reporting, and none is documented in the province.
tangentialFactors: No province-level turbulence, emergency measure or local campaign targeting trans residents was identified for North Maluku. The provinces that add their own criminalisation sit outside this one, so a visitor's exposure here is the national one, without a sub-national overlay.
localsOnly: No province-specific service, protection or enforcement practice for trans residents in North Maluku was identified. Residents' legal position, document route and exposure to the penal code are set at the national level.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether North Maluku is among the provinces covered by the national home affairs ministry's electronic ID card outreach for transgender residents, begun in June 2021 across nine provinces, is not stated in the sources.

No province-level enforcement statistics, court records or municipal ordinances on dress, facilities or public morality were located for North Maluku. Whether any district within the province has issued its own morality regulation is unresolved.
